title: Unique Paths
prompt:
A robot starts at the top-left of an `m x n` grid and moves only right or down. How many distinct paths reach the bottom-right? (Answers fit in int.)

**Example**: `m = 3, n = 7` → `28`.

You drilled this exact table in the pattern lesson — now it's the real problem.
hints: dp[i][j] = paths into cell (i, j) = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1].
First row and first column are all 1 — only one straight-line way in.
Bonus: a single 1-D row array suffices, updated left to right.

solution.explanation: The rolled 1-D version: before assignment, `dp[j]` still holds the value from the row above and `dp[j-1]` is already this row's left neighbor. O(m·n) time, O(n) space. (The full 2-D table from the drill is equally accepted.)
